public_rationale: Under the stated practical-service reading, the forecast is supported. By May 5, 2025, Waymo reported more than 250,000 paid weekly trips across four cities. Previously published research covering 25.3 million driverless miles found substantially fewer liability claims than its human-driving benchmarks. Together, these meet the early-resolution rule. The result depends on reading arrival as established commercial usefulness; it does not establish universal availability or flawless driving.
limitations: Marcus supplied no explicit adoption threshold, so interpretation materially affects the result.
The safety research includes Waymo authors and measures insurance liability claims rather than every aspect of service reliability.
The evidence concerns bounded operating areas.

statement.excerpt: I—truly a techno-optimist, popular perceptions to the contrary—do think driverless will come, eventually.
statement.document_title: Why driverless cars might—or might not—be at the end of the road

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that driverless cars become an established, usable transport service.
Because the surrounding passage acknowledges existing driverless activity and discusses reliability, a demonstration or first limited pilot is insufficient.
I treat sustained commercial service across multiple cities, at substantial recurring passenger volume and with measured real-world safety performance, as practical arrival.
Marcus does not require universal geographic coverage, private ownership, zero crashes, or the absence of all remote assistance.
The adjacent claim about eventually being safer than humans informs the context but is not treated as a separate universal safety guarantee.
criteria.support_condition: Documented deployments establish sustained public commercial transport without a supervising driver, at substantial recurring scale, accompanied by real-world evidence supporting practical reliability.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence establishes that driverless transport as described is impossible. Failure to reach it by any unstated date does not contradict eventual arrival.

evidence.excerpt: Waymo One has grown substantially in the last couple of years.
evidence.locator: Section 'Tooling up for growth'; opening paragraph supplies weekly trips and cities
evidence.explanation: The disclosure reports more than 250,000 paid weekly trips across Phoenix, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Austin, with over 1,500 commercial vehicles. This establishes recurring practical deployment well beyond a demonstration.

evidence.excerpt:
Compared to the overall driving population there was an 88% reduction in property damage claims and
a 92% reduction in bodily injury claims.
evidence.locator: Key findings, second page; 'Waymo ADS Data' identifies the observation period
evidence.explanation: The study covers 25.3 million driverless miles through July 31, 2024, with claims evaluated through November 30. Its geographically adjusted insurance comparison supports practical safety within the deployed operating areas.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The dated disclosure establishes substantial recurring commercial driverless service in four cities; e2 supplies the previously available real-world safety evidence required by the rule.
